blocks.prompt: 5. Differentiate with respect to the variable involved: \(y = (1 + \csc t)\sin t\)
blocks.explanation:
Variable phir \(t\) hai, to \(\frac{dy}{dt}\) chahiye.
Diya kya hai? \(y = (1 + \csc t)\sin t\): ek bracket aur \(\sin t\) ka product.
Rule kaunsa? Product rule. Lekin ek samajhdar teacher pehle yeh bhi dekhta hai ke kya function ko pehle hi aasaan kiya ja sakta hai.
Plan: kitab ke tareeqe se product rule lagayenge, phir \(\csc t\sin t = 1\) se simplify karenge; aakhir mein aasaan raste se tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = (1 + \csc t)\sin t\), jahan \(\sin t \neq 0\).
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dt}\).
Tareeqa: product rule, \(u = 1 + \csc t\), \(v = \sin t\). \(\sin t \neq 0\) isliye ke \(\csc t = \frac{1}{\sin t}\) wahan define hi nahi.

Product rule lagayein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dt} = (1 + \csc t)'\sin t\]
\[\quad + (1 + \csc t)(\sin t)'\]
Kyun: \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\): pehle bracket ka derivative darja \(\sin t\), plus bracket darja \(\sin t\) ka derivative.

Derivatives rakhein
\[= (-\csc t\cot t)\sin t + (1 + \csc t)\cos t\]
Kyun: \(1\) constant hai to derivative 0; \((\csc t)' = -\csc t\cot t\) (Question 1(b) wala, minus ke saath!); \((\sin t)' = \cos t\).

Simplify karein
\[\csc t\sin t = 1,\quad \csc t\cos t = \cot t\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\cot t + \cos t + \cot t\]
\[= \cos t\]
Kyun: \(\csc t = \frac{1}{\sin t}\), to \(\csc t\sin t = 1\), aur \(\csc t\cos t = \frac{\cos t}{\sin t} = \cot t\). Pehli term \(-\cot t\) bani, bracket kholne par \(\cos t + \cot t\) aaya, aur \(-\cot t\) aur \(+\cot t\) cancel ho gaye.

Tasdeeq: pehle simplify kar ke
\[y = \sin t + \csc t\sin t = \sin t + 1\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \cos t\]
Kyun: bracket pehle hi khol dein to \(\csc t\sin t = 1\) se function sirf \(\sin t + 1\) reh jata hai, jis ka derivative ek line mein \(\cos t\) hai. Sabaq: differentiate karne se pehle hamesha dekhiye ke function aasaan ho sakta hai ya nahi; waqt bhi bachta hai aur ghalti ka chance bhi kam hota hai.
